clue.text: Equipment for sport — bet it cracks in use!

indicators.note: put to use, the letters of the phrase are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A gambler wagers that some piece of sports kit will break once it is used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in use' tells you to rearrange BET IT CRACKS; cricket is England's summer bat-and-ball game, and its bats do crack with heavy use.
explanation.definitionFit: Willow bats are the gear a cricketer carries to the crease.

clue.text: Dependable, but can tire badly

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of can and tire end up jumbled

explanation.surface: Something is reliable, though a can may tire out badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' signals an anagram of CAN plus TIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sure to happen or reliable can be described as dependable, a near synonym.

clue.text: Road up — time to make representation!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the road's letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, written MI in crosswords
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A road is dug up and it is time to make a picture of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the motorway in this down light; the M1 runs from London to Leeds and is the crossword's usual road.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture or likeness is a representation of something.

clue.text: Some Yankee personality's attendants

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the staff around an American celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' points to letters inside yanKEE PERSonality's.
explanation.definitionFit: Keepers look after things or people, as attendants do in a museum or zoo.

clue.text: Catsuit fashioned for notable old Roman

indicators.note: something fashioned is shaped anew, so the letters of catsuit are remade

explanation.surface: A catsuit is styled for a famous figure from ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' signals an anagram of CATSUIT; Tacitus was a Roman historian.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a celebrated historian of imperial Rome.

clue.text: Bill made certain allegations — should be commended

parts.note: a bill is an account, abbreviated AC
to claim is to allege, so making allegations is having claimed

explanation.surface: A man named Bill made definite charges and deserves praise for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hailed and praised publicly is to be commended.

clue.text: The individual observing a quarter fiddle

parts.note: south is one quarter of the compass, abbreviated S
to potter is to fiddle about aimlessly

explanation.surface: Someone watches a person who spends a quarter of the time messing around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' suggests a violin or a fraud, but here it means to tinker or potter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotter is a person who watches out for things, such as trains or birds.

clue.text: Concern about a label showing the cost of transport

indicators.note: about means going around, so concern's synonym surrounds the label word

parts.note: concern and care both mean worry or attention
a tag is a label tied to something

explanation.surface: A worry over what a price tag shows about the shipping cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals a container; the 'a' before 'label' is only an article and adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartage is the charge for carrying goods by cart or lorry.

clue.text: An ill-natured musician, expert with the arbalest

parts.note: cross means bad-tempered
a string player who draws a bow across the strings may be called a bowman

explanation.surface: A grumpy musician turns out to be skilled with an old weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: An arbalest is a medieval crossbow; 'musician' is a whimsical name for a player who bows a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbalest is a medieval crossbow, so someone expert with one shoots it.

clue.text: This great man would take the central view

definitions.text: This great man would take the central view

parts.words: This great man would take the central view
parts.note: a giant of Greek myth with one eye in the middle of his forehead sees only from the centre; 'central view' sounds political

explanation.surface: A great statesman would adopt a moderate, middle-of-the-road position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central view' reads like a centrist opinion; it is the outlook of a one-eyed mythic giant.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-eyed giants of Greek myth have a single eye in the middle of the forehead.

clue.text: Taking a night's rest diminishes wrinkles!

indicators.note: taking the letters of the phrase and rearranging them into new order

explanation.surface: A good night's sleep is said to smooth out the lines on your face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' is an unusual anagram signal for A NIGHTS REST.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooth creases out of cloth or skin is to reduce its wrinkles.

clue.text: Love speed, and so speak out

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Love speeds up, and so a person declares their feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is a tennis score of nil, the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim or hold forth in public is to speak out.

clue.text: A fan of old farm machinery

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a tractor is the main farm vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone is an enthusiast for vintage farm vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fan' looks like an enthusiast; it is the device that clears steam from a kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor is the kind of fan that draws stale air out of a room.

clue.text: Having no boys to disrupt lessons

indicators.note: disrupting the letters of lessons throws them into a new order

explanation.surface: With no sons, there are none to disrupt the classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to disrupt' signals an anagram of LESSONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sons are male children, so lacking them leaves a parent with only daughters or none.

clue.text: The promptitude of an aristocrat in letter writing

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
the letter S written out as a word is ess

explanation.surface: A nobleman's prompt replies to his correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter writing' means writing out the name of the letter S in full, ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Promptitude means punctuality or being early to act.

clue.text: Some Japanese will give one a drink when retiring

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the whole string of pieces is read from right to left

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
rum is a spirit
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Some Japanese people will offer a drink at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reverses I A RUM AS to give the warriors; samurai are the warrior class of old Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: The samurai were the hereditary warrior caste of feudal Japan.

clue.text: Presented from before 500

parts.note: off means away from, as in 'off the shelf'
ere is an old word for before
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Something was shown from before the year 500.
explanation.walkthrough: '500' is the Roman numeral D.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to hold it out for acceptance.

clue.text: Expression of disgust about a head's cunning

indicators.note: about means going around, so the exclamation wraps round the headland

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a head teacher's crafty manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals a container; 'head' is not a person but a headland, as in place names such as Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is skill and subtlety in handling things, a kind of artful craft.

clue.text: The conscript has to get primitive craft into the river

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other, the vessel inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a British river
a raft is a basic boat made of logs

explanation.surface: A conscripted man must get a crude boat onto the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals a container; the Dee is a river flowing through Wales, England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is someone called up for military service.

clue.text: The German returns food that's coloured pink

indicators.note: returns means the German word is sent back, read right to left

parts.note: der is a German word for the
a dish is a prepared food

explanation.surface: A German brings back a meal that has a rosy colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses the German article, which neatly supplies the colour itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink is a pale shade near red, so something pinkish is somewhat red.

clue.text: Go in for further education, respecting coaches

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a train is a line of railway coaches

explanation.surface: Someone takes a new course with respect to how they coach others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coaches' looks like a verb about teaching, but it is railway carriages, a TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn new skills for a fresh job is to undergo further schooling.

clue.text: A rascal put over others will get money advanced

indicators.note: in a down clue, put over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A scoundrel lords it over others and gets an advance of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put over' places IMP above REST in the down light; an imprest is a cash advance for official spending.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprest is a sum of cash advanced to someone for official spending.

clue.text: A fellow without means unable to better himself?

parts.note: to mend is to improve, as in 'mend your ways'
unable is saying 'I can't'

explanation.surface: A poor man cannot improve his lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads as the beggar's lament 'Mend? I can't', which the clue words say in a different order.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is a beggar, someone who lives on alms.

clue.text: Wood — there's ample available

indicators.note: available here means the letters are on hand to be rearranged

explanation.surface: There is plenty of timber to be had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'available' is a loose anagram signal for AMPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple is a hardwood timber from a tree with lobed leaves.

clue.text: Maxim that would be outrageous in a doctor

indicators.note: in means the outrageous piece sits inside the doctor's letters

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
OTT stands for over the top, meaning outrageous

explanation.surface: A saying that would sound scandalous coming from a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals a container; OTT, short for over the top, is everyday British slang for excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A short guiding saying such as a family's watchword is a maxim.

clue.text: Set one's heart on a perfume now in production

indicators.note: on means the middle letter is placed first, on the rest
the heart of a word is its middle letter, here the centre of one's

parts.note: a scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: Someone has fallen for a fragrance that has just been launched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's heart' is the middle letter N, and 'on' sets it before A SCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is just coming into existence, newly being made.

clue.text: She's always ready to play her part

definitions.text: She's always ready to play her part

parts.words: She's always ready to play her part
parts.note: a woman who is always willing to do her bit, read literally as one who performs roles on stage

explanation.surface: A dependable woman is always willing to do her share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play her part' reads as doing her bit; it literally means performing a role.
explanation.definitionFit: A female performer takes roles in plays and films.

clue.text: As far to the right as can be — on paper

definitions.text: As far to the right as can be — on paper

parts.words: As far to the right as can be — on paper
parts.note: maps are printed with north at the top, so the extreme right of the paper is the furthest point in one compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone holds the most right-wing views possible, at least in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' suggests politics, and 'on paper' suggests in theory; on a map the right edge is the east.
explanation.definitionFit: On a map, right is east, so the rightmost point lies farthest towards sunrise.
